hta_trace: full-utf8.hta is byte-identical to normalized.hta after removing the 13-byte %codigo_js% CRLF builder placeholder. No additional encoded executable is present.
The HTA declares InternalCache, no border/caption/system menu/taskbar entry and minimized state. JScript immediately requests zero-size and negative-position windows.

window.onload calls RunPayload. It constructs MSXML2.ServerXMLHTTP.6.0, opens a synchronous GET for https://imperiailmports.com/yCkifY0p, sends, stores responseText in flybane and directly evaluates that same variable. Empty catch swallows failures; window.close follows.

Concealment plus unverified automatic privileged remote code evaluation, with no useful cache UI or normal application task, establishes a concealed loader. The ultimate payload, successful execution, initial delivery and victim authorization are unknown; no malware family is inferred.

Both separate hostile claims remain: payload script evaluation and concealment of its execution. Every other firing observation corresponds to literal HTA configuration, COM/network/eval operations, empty error handling, window manipulation or file identity.
html_trace: Actual file is a GitHub HTML blob page, not a PowerShell script. All fourteen script elements are external GitHub module loads, an importmap, or application/json data; there is no executable inline script, event-handler attribute or javascript: URL.

The JSON rawLines field and rendered divs display 947 lines of PowerShell. Forager recovered the independently scanned raw link at SHA256 8ef32cf815363f34936e1950d15a08e2dee09208e815271444116c8c9c74fa88; every displayed source line matches. Its .forage.json provenance is retained in scratch.

PowerShell behavior: Twitter timeline response -> LatestTweet -> switch -> cmd /C evaluation; tweet-selected local file -> ReadAllBytes -> Base64 -> Pastebin UploadValues; screenshot and credential-prompt capture; downloaded startup shortcut stager; network/cmd stream relay; LSASS token impersonation; key-state polling and file logging. These source capabilities remain detected and are not claims that the HTML runs them.

Base64 startup command decodes to $A = GC $env:ProgramData\cache.db; IEX $A. The other deliberate blob is the standard EICAR test signature. Numeric character casts implement volume-key sends; JSON Unicode escapes are serialization, not an attack on this page.

Loading raw source only defines Invoke-TwitterBot. Explicit invocation enters the loop; its 2013-02-16 kill date precedes network tasking. IP/work-hour guards also apply. GetSystem, BindShell and KeyLog definitions do not match the dispatcher names GetSystemCommand, BindShellCommand and KeylogCommand. These limits do not erase the implemented attack capabilities.

Conference research provenance and inert source-view packaging tip the supplied HTML to BENIGN. The raw source is a separate attack-capable artifact; its accurate hostile/suspicious rules are retained. No claim is made about victim deployment or authorization.

correction.unsupported_claim: The actual saved page text #Convert password to plaintext was described as displaying a literal password. Bare password-to prose supplies neither a value label nor a value.
correction.change: Require is or colon before the short inline value, allowing an optional purpose phrase such as to open the file. Keep the same notable criticality, platform/type scope, ID, placement and HTML-comment exclusion. No package/identity exception or severity reduction.
correction.positive_review: Inspected all three consumers and existing out-of-batch HTML ZIP and reversed-fragment positive fixtures. No pre-existing HTML positive for the password-value atom was found by a repository search. Added explicit password-bearing controls for all three consumers, including a real encrypted ZIP containing harmless notice.txt. The fragmented control derives from the existing attack fixture. The real supplied GitHub page, not a synthetic near miss alone, establishes the false positive.
correction.retained_coverage: 15 boundary cases pass: direct/tagged/purpose values, all three attack consumers, conversion/instruction prose, empty form labels, HTML comments, and existing out-of-batch controls. Also 16 existing HTA cases and 13 existing TwitterBot cases pass.
correction.material_detection_losses: Only the false literal-password claim disappears from the supplied page. Its attack consumers no longer fire on conversion prose in corresponding controls. All intended positive controls remain detected. No original hostile or suspicious finding was lost; no criticality changed.

dependency_confirmation.note: No YAML change to any dependency finding; isolated before/after scans include its decoded PowerShell child. Reference-following continues to propagate the raw source verdict to the HTML although the page does not execute that source.

classifier_gaps: Both malicious HTAs retain two hostile rules each and probability 0.9938969, but calibrated ML level remains -1. This calibration miss was not manipulated with new or duplicate rules.

The benign page has no local hostile/suspicious YAML finding before or after; local ML probability is 0.5578971 -> 0.575994, calibrated level -1. Reference-following still reports 0.98 at level 25 via the raw source, not an executing HTML dependency. This propagation disagreement requires engine/context handling rather than weakening correct raw-source traits.

reference_following_comparison.other_changes: Follow-up reference traversal analyzes previously incomplete GitHub asset records and one additional Unicode-decoded JavaScript content hash. These are extra coverage, not effects attributed to the password matcher. No original content hash or additional trait was lost.

final_check: make validate is required after these records and markers are written; its result is reported in the conversation.
